column3: The Hebrew retains the title term Nehiloth; BSB interprets it as accompaniment by flutes.
The Hebrew leaves what he arranges unnamed; BSB supplies my plea.
The Hebrew names His eyes rather than presence.
The Hebrew has his mouth, then their inward part; throat, grave, and tongue are singular, where BSB uses plural throats, graves, and tongues.
The Hebrew has a singular righteous person and him; BSB uses them.
